test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 21 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 minutes, while pipe B can empty the completely filled tank in 24 minutes. Initially, pipe A is opened and after 4 minutes, pipe B is also opened. In how much time (in minutes) will the remaining tank be filled completely?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A fills 1/12 per min ⇒ in 4 min fills 1/3

Remaining = 2/3

Net rate (A+B) = 1/12 − 1/24 = 1/24

Time for remaining = (2/3) ÷ (1/24) = 16 min

**∴ Answer = 16 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Pipe A = 12 min, Pipe B = 24 min

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 Pipe
 Time (min)
 Total Work
 Efficiency
 
 
 
 

 A (Fill)
 12
 24
 2
 
 

 B (Empty)
 24
 −1
 
 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Work done by A in 4 min = 4 × 2 = 8 units

⇒ Remaining work = 24 − 8 = 16 units

⇒ Net efficiency (A+B) = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/min

⇒ Time = 16 ÷ 1 = 16 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 16 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes Concept

Filling is positive work, emptying is negative.

Partial Work

First find work done before second pipe starts.

Net Efficiency

Add/subtract efficiencies to get final rate.
